subject: history_social
passage: The Italian Jesuit Matteo Ricci arrived in China in 1582 and spent nearly three decades there, eventually mastering classical Chinese. He had studied mathematics and astronomy in Rome before sailing east. Working with Chinese scholars, including the mathematician Li Zhizao, he produced a world map that combined European geographic knowledge with Chinese sources and place names. Printed in Beijing in 1602 on six large panels, ______ a choice that most likely made the unfamiliar map more acceptable to its Chinese readers.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the map placed China near the center rather than at the edge, as many European maps did,
choices.B: Ricci and his collaborators placed China near the center rather than at the edge, as many European maps did,
choices.C: Ricci's decision placed China near the center rather than at the edge, as many European maps did,
choices.D: China was placed near the center rather than at the edge, as many European maps did,

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Printed in Beijing in 1602 on six large panels" can describe only the map. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be "the map."
explanation.A: Correct. "The map" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that the map was what was printed on six panels.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This makes "Ricci and his collaborators" the subject, so the sentence says the people were printed on six panels.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The subject is "decision"; a decision cannot be printed on panels.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes "China" the subject, so the sentence says the country was printed in Beijing on six panels.
